case.title: POSCO Future M: Korean owner, Chinese graphite
case.subtitle: POSCO Future M Co., Ltd. · Sejong and Pohang, South Korea
case.question: Could Sayari tell a non-Chinese-owned anode supplier that uses Chinese graphite apart from a Chinese-owned one?
case.headline: Yes on ownership, partly on inputs. Sayari's Korean registry data shows POSCO Holdings owns 58.2% of POSCO Future M, with no Chinese owner anywhere up the chain. It also shows Chinese natural graphite going in (to Dec 2023) and 95 anode shipments going out to GM, SK Battery America, Tesla, Panasonic and XALT (Dec 2021 – Jul 2026). It cannot show how much Chinese graphite ends up in any US-bound shipment, and its Chinese input trail stops in Dec 2023, while the company says it still uses Chinese spherical graphite.
case.summary_for_non_experts: POSCO Future M is the battery-materials arm of Korea's POSCO steel group. It is the largest anode maker outside China and sells to US battery and car plants. This is our contrast case: the owner is Korean, but the company has relied on China for spherical graphite, the rounded, purified graphite that natural-graphite anode is made from. Sayari shows the Korean owner clearly, unlike BTR's Indonesian plant in Case 1, and it shows Chinese graphite going in and anode going out to the US. What it cannot show is how much Chinese material is inside the anode that reaches the US.

steps.title: One company, one registry anchor
steps.text: Sayari holds about a dozen records for POSCO Future M under its old and new names. The main one carries Korea's DART disclosure ID, so the anchor is solid. Other records share its Pohang or Gwangyang street address; two are name-only and kept as leads.

steps.title: The owner is in the registry
steps.text: Korea's disclosure data, as held by Sayari, names POSCO Holdings as owner of 58.2%. Every other shareholder is Korean, including the National Pension Service. This is the question the US PFE rules ask first, and here Sayari answers it directly. In Case 1 it could not.

steps.title: Chinese graphite in
steps.text: Natural graphite (HS 2504) arrived from Zhanjiang Juxin and three Qingdao suppliers in 2023, and artificial graphite (HS 3801) from Qingdao Kuntuo and Qingdao Qingbei Carbon. POSCO Future M is the top Korean buyer of Chinese 'spherical graphite' in Sayari, with 167 shipments. Smaller inputs came from Mozambique, Germany and the UK.

steps.title: Anode out to US plants
steps.text: 105 shipment rows of HS 3801 left Korea for the US. 95 went to battery or car makers: GM (37), SK Battery America (32), Tesla (13), Panasonic Energy (9) and XALT Energy (4). The rest went to freight forwarders and one electrode maker. The company has also announced an anode deal with Ultium Cells, but Sayari's rows name GM as the consignee.

steps.title: What the data can't separate
steps.text: Trade rows can't link a Chinese input to a US-bound export, or tell Sejong's natural-graphite anode from Pohang's artificial-graphite anode. Chinese graphite rows to POSCO Future M stop on 8 Dec 2023, a week after China's export licensing began. The company says it still uses Chinese spherical graphite, so the gap is in coverage. Several name-and-HS searches returned 0 even though the graph holds the flows.

detected.text: Korean ownership: POSCO Holdings holds 58.2% (registry record); no Chinese owner on any of 50 ownership paths.
Chinese natural and artificial graphite shipped into POSCO Future M by named Chinese suppliers, Oct 2021 – Dec 2023.
95 dated rows of anode material to GM, SK Battery America, Tesla, Panasonic Energy and XALT Energy, Dec 2021 – Jul 2026.

suggested.text: Continued dependence on Chinese spherical graphite after 2023: stated by the company in the press, not visible in Sayari after 8 Dec 2023.
Anode supply to Ultium Cells: announced by the company; Sayari shows the shipments under GM's name.

not_visible.text: How much Chinese-origin graphite is inside any US-bound shipment. This is the 'material assistance' share the PFE rules weigh, separately from ownership.
Which plant (Sejong natural, Pohang artificial) made each US shipment. Product codes such as PAS-C3B and PAS-CP3K are not explained in the data.
Who the Chinese graphite suppliers are owned by. We did not trace them; under the PFE rules that could matter more than POSCO's own ownership.

red_flags.flag: Chinese parent ownership of the transit plant
red_flags.note: Checked and absent: the registry shows a Korean parent (POSCO Holdings, 58.2%).

red_flags.flag: Same HS imported from China and exported to the US
red_flags.note: HS 3801 in from Qingdao suppliers (2021–2023); HS 3801 out to US cell plants. Normal for a processor; the main input is natural graphite (HS 2504).

red_flags.flag: Recent incorporation vs. first export date
red_flags.note: Checked and absent: registered 1971, decades before its first anode exports.

red_flags.flag: Volume spike after a policy date
red_flags.note: No spike in our rows. The buyer mix shifts: GM to Jun 2024, SK Battery America to Jun 2025, Tesla and Panasonic in 2026.

red_flags.flag: Shared address or officer with a flagged entity
red_flags.note: None found. Watchlist hits are two hops out through big trading partners (noise).
About a dozen records under two company names; anchored by a DART ID.
Main record is 'adjacent' to a Sheffield Hallam-named entity; one Laixi supplier carries the same flag. Context, not a finding.

caveats: Using Chinese graphite in Korea is legal and common. Nothing here shows wrongdoing by any company named.
The US buyers are named because they appear in customs records; this says nothing about their compliance.
Entity-resolution links are our judgment and could be wrong.
HS 3801 also covers non-battery graphite. POSCO's sister steel company imports Chinese 'recarburizer' under HS 3801.10, a steelmaking additive; we excluded it.
Chinese input rows come from Chinese export data and stop in Dec 2023 for this buyer. Korea's own import records are not in our results, so later inputs may be missing.
Several product rows are miscoded (e.g. anode material under textile or photo-film HS codes); we counted them only where the text says anode material.

calls.question: Which Sayari records are POSCO Future M?
calls.purpose: Resolve the company and its fragments
calls.result_summary: 19 records. The main one (株式会社POSCO CHEMICAL, DART CIK 00155276) carries both the old and new names and addresses in Pohang, Gwangyang and Sejong. At least ten more records use the POSCO Future M or POSCO Chemical name, several with the same Pohang (110 Sinhang-ro) or Gwangyang (45 Yulchonsandan 8-ro) street addresses. Two records name the freight forwarder LX Pantos acting for POSCO Future M; one is the Canadian subsidiary in Bécancour.
calls.interpretation: Unlike Case 1, the main record has a registry identifier (Korea's DART disclosure ID), so the anchor is solid. Same-address fragments are treated as 'possibly the same as'.

calls.question: Who owns POSCO Future M, and who does it trade with?
calls.purpose: Ownership and trade partners of the main record
calls.result_summary: Registered 1971-05-13. Business purpose includes refractories and secondary-battery manufacturing. Shareholder: 포스코홀딩스(주) (POSCO Holdings) with 58.2%, from Korea's DART disclosure database. Owns the Canadian subsidiary. Trade counts: 10,199 sent, 1,788 received. Ships to Tesla, VinFast and a Polish logistics agent; receives from Huayou New Energy (Quzhou) and a Shanghai supply-chain firm.
calls.interpretation: Ownership is a registry record with a percentage. The parent is Korean. This is the opposite of Case 1, where Sayari had no owner for BTR's plant.

calls.question: Is there any Chinese owner anywhere up the chain?
calls.result_summary: 50 owner paths returned, all one hop and all Korean: POSCO Holdings (three records under Korean and English names), POSCO (주)포스코, the National Pension Service (국민연금공단), Pohang University of Science and Technology, and about 40 named Korean individuals (DART shareholding filings by officers).
calls.interpretation: No Chinese owner appears at any level. The individual names are officers who report small holdings; they are not controlling owners.

calls.question: Where do POSCO Future M's graphite and carbon inputs come from?
calls.result_summary: 18 supplier rows. Natural graphite (HS 2504) from China: Zhanjiang Juxin New Energy (two records, Jul–Dec 2023), Qingdao Haida New Energy Materials (Jun–Sep 2023), Qingdao Zhongshuo New Energy (Aug 2023), Qingdao Kuntuo New Material (Jul–Sep 2023). Artificial graphite (HS 3801) from China: Qingdao Kuntuo (Sep 2023) and Qingdao Qingbei Carbon Products (Oct 2021 – Jul 2022). Natural graphite from Twigg Exploration & Mining, Mozambique (Jun 2022). Petroleum coke (HS 2713) from China EPT (Jul 2022) and P66 Ltd, UK (Mar 2022). Coal-tar pitch and oils from Rain Carbon Germany via Belgium and the Netherlands (Nov 2021 – Jan 2024). Carbon black (HS 2803) from several of the Qingdao and Zhanjiang suppliers.
calls.interpretation: Chinese natural graphite does flow into this Korean-owned producer. Every Chinese graphite row is dated 2023 or earlier.

calls.result_summary: 0 rows.
calls.interpretation: The same flows s404 found are not reachable by name plus HS plus corridor. Shipment search and the supply-chain graph disagree. Recorded as a tool finding.

calls.result_summary: 0 rows.

calls.question: Who are all of POSCO Future M's Chinese suppliers in the graph?
calls.result_summary: 44 China-linked suppliers. Graphite-related names include Zhanjiang Juxin New Energy (Guandu Industrial Park, Zhanjiang), Qingdao Huateng Graphite Technology (Nanshu Town, Laixi), Qingdao GR-Taida Carbon (Pingdu), Qingdao Luowei New Material (Graphite New Material Cluster Area, Nanshu, Laixi), Qingdao Qingbei Carbon Products (same Laixi graphite cluster), Qingdao Kuntuo New Material (Nanshu, Laixi), Hunan Zoomwe Zhengyuan Advanced Material Trade (four records) and Nantong Jintong Energy Storage. Others supply cathode inputs (Huayou New Energy Quzhou in several records, Zhejiang POSCO Huayou ESM, Ganfeng Lithium, Tianqi Lithium, Yibin Tianyi Lithium), refractories (Zibo Luzhong, Yingkou Zhonghe, RHI Asia Pacific) or are freight forwarders (Kuehne + Nagel, Shanghai Speedy, Global Expedition Logistics).
calls.interpretation: Several graphite suppliers sit in the Nanshu/Laixi natural-graphite cluster in Shandong. The list mixes battery, cathode and steel-refractory inputs, because the company also makes refractories.

calls.question: Does POSCO Future M ship anode material to US battery makers?
calls.result_summary: 105 rows in total; this page has 40. Supplier is the main POSCO Future M record on every row. Buyers on this page: Tesla (12 rows of artificial graphite HS 3801.10, 'anode active material', Jan–Feb 2026), Panasonic Energy Corporation (9 rows, HS 3801.90 and 3801.10, 'anode active material', May–Jul 2026), SK Battery America (8 rows, 'Graphite PAS-CP3K', May–Jun 2025), General Motors LLC (1 row HS 3801.10, Dec 2021), Tesla with Panasonic Procurement Corporation of America (1 row, Aug 2023), and two freight forwarders, Scan Global Logistics DTW (8 rows, 2023) and FNS Inc. Chicago (1 row, 2023).
calls.interpretation: The query-text method from Case 1 works: every row's supplier is the right company, and product text says 'anode active material'.

calls.question: What are those May 2026 rows?
calls.purpose: Check product text before counting it as anode input
calls.result_summary: Shipper: Tianjin Eboxline International Transport. Buyer: 'POSCO CO LTD' at 6261 Donghaean-ro (the Pohang steelworks). calls.result_summary: KED Global: Korea relies entirely on Chinese imports for natural and spherical graphite; POSCO Future M plans to make spherical graphite at home. Korea Herald: the Sejong plant 'currently reprocesses spherical graphite … imported from China' and aims to phase out Chinese intermediates by 2027; a new Saemangeum plant (subsidiary Future Graph) will use African graphite. POSCO E&C: Sejong makes natural-graphite anode. POSCO newsroom: same Africa → Saemangeum → Sejong plan.
